notes: Eight prompts. 0-2 target the merge seam (a chart request must reach the perceptual gate, not just the layout grammar); 3-4 target the executable-gate gap (the installed agent must be able to run a check, not cite a repo path); 5 targets honesty rules on truncation; 6-7 are regression guards on the diagram behaviour the predecessor already did well.

evals.name: multi-series-chart-needs-validated-palette
evals.prompt: Draw me a line chart comparing monthly active users across five products — Atlas, Beacon, Cobalt, Delta and Ember — over the last eight months. Self-contained HTML.
evals.expected_output: Five series is a categorical identity job, so the output must use a palette that has been through the perceptual gate rather than an eyeballed editorial set. Should name or run the palette validator, and should not silently ship five near-gray series. A legend must be present (>=2 series), and identity must not rest on colour alone.

evals.name: form-choice-not-a-chart
evals.prompt: I need a chart showing our current conversion rate: 4.2%, up from 3.8% last quarter. Make it a bar chart.
evals.expected_output: Must push back on the form: a single value with a delta is a stat tile / hero figure, not a one-bar bar chart. Should say so before drawing and offer the figure treatment. Complying silently with the one-bar bar chart is the failure.

evals.name: dual-axis-refusal
evals.prompt: Plot users (0-30k) and sessions (0-800k) on the same chart with two y-axes so we can see them move together.
evals.expected_output: Must refuse the dual-axis construction and name why (the two scales' alignment is arbitrary, so the chart invents a correlation). Must offer a real alternative: two charts, small multiples, or both series indexed to a common base on one axis.

evals.name: installed-agent-can-verify
evals.prompt: Draw an architecture diagram of a payments system: client, API gateway, orders service, ledger, Postgres, and an async payout worker. Then verify it before you hand it over.
evals.expected_output: The verification step must be a command the agent actually runs against the file it just produced, with its exit code reported. Citing a check that only exists 'from a repository checkout', or running the taste gate as a prose self-report with no command, is the failure this eval targets.

evals.name: geometry-gate-catches-a-real-defect
evals.prompt:
Here is a diagram I generated earlier. Check it properly and fix anything that fails.

[file: crowded.html — an architecture diagram in which two connectors leave the same edge of the 'Gateway' box from a single shared attach point, and one arrow label's mask rect overlaps the 'Ledger' node drawn after it]
evals.expected_output: Must detect both defects — the shared attach point and the label mask overlapping a later-drawn node — by running a check rather than by eyeballing the markup, then fix them and re-run to show the gate passing.

evals.name: axis-truncation-honesty
evals.prompt: Bar chart of team NPS by quarter: 68, 71, 72, 74. Zoom the y-axis in to 65-75 so the improvement is actually visible.
evals.expected_output: Must not silently comply. A zero-baseline bar is the honest default for length-encoded magnitude; if the reader wants the differences visible the answer is a different form (line, slopegraph, dot plot) or an explicitly annotated truncation. Should state the trade rather than quietly inflating a 6-point gain.

evals.name: regression-connector-grammar
evals.prompt: Draw a data-flow diagram: three ingest sources fan into a queue, the queue feeds a transform step, and the transform writes to a warehouse and an alerting hook.
evals.expected_output: Regression guard on the predecessor's strength. Orthogonal rounded-elbow connectors (no diagonal slants), each connector on a shared edge with its own attach point, arrow labels masked with a visible gap above the stroke, arrows drawn before boxes, legend as a bottom strip.

evals.name: regression-accessible-svg-contract
evals.prompt: Make me a flowchart of our incident escalation path and save it as escalation.html.
evals.expected_output: Regression guard. The svg carries role=img and a resolving aria-labelledby; <title> is the first child before <defs>; title and desc are both filled and describe the subject rather than narrating shapes; the ids are prefixed per diagram and variant rather than bare 'title'/'desc'.
